state: JevCode automation design, round 9. The operator wants the site to 'flow': scheduled jobs that periodically (1) fetch/crawl new source material (official docs updates from docs.typesafe.ai, ecosystem GitHub star counts, new community projects), (2) prepare updated/new content, (3) use Jev to JUDGE what content to publish, where it belongs (which section/language), and WHEN to publish it, then (4) auto-deploy approved items. Current infrastructure facts: static Astro site on a VPS with atomic symlink deploys; repo is PUBLIC on GitHub (miounet11/jevcode) with Actions available; the deploy requires SSH to the VPS which Actions cannot do without storing the SSH key as a repo secret; local machine (macOS, has cron) has full deploy capability and the TYPESAFE_API_KEY in .env; content is markdown in src/content/docs with 8 languages; ecosystem data (stars) was last collected 2026-09-18, one day ago. Jev's role: it is a judgment model (typed noul/choice/score outputs, no prose generation) — suitable for gatekeeping decisions like 'is this update worth publishing', 'is this draft ready', 'what category does this belong to', NOT for writing content. Design questions follow.

scheduler_choice.instructions: Where should the scheduled pipeline run?

criteria.local_cron: macOS launchd/cron on the operator's machine: has SSH key, API key, deploy access; simplest; runs only when machine is on
criteria.github_actions: GitHub Actions scheduled workflow: runs in cloud reliably; needs repo secrets (API key) but CANNOT deploy to VPS without adding an SSH secret too
criteria.vps_cron: Cron on the VPS itself: always-on, has the site; needs API key copied there and the repo cloned there; deploy is local symlink switch
criteria.hybrid: GitHub Actions for fetch+judge+commit, VPS-side hook (or manual pull) for deploy

pipeline_stages.instructions: Which pipeline stages should be automated in v1?

criteria.stars_only: V1 = ecosystem star refresh only (mechanical data update, no editorial judgment needed)
criteria.stars_plus_detect: V1 = star refresh + change detection on docs.typesafe.ai (diff the llms.txt index and page hashes) + Jev gate on whether changes are worth a content update
criteria.full_loop: V1 = fetch + Jev gate + content prep + Jev publish-when gate + auto deploy, all stages
criteria.content_drafts: V1 = Jev-judged publishing of human-prepared content drafts only (no crawling)

jev_gate_design.instructions: How should Jev be used in the publish gate?

criteria.two_stage: Two Jev calls: gate-1 at intake (is this change significant enough to publish? noul + category choice), gate-2 at release (is the assembled release coherent? noul + score) — matches the model's typed-judgment strengths
criteria.single_gate: One Jev call at release time only: publish/hold/escalate choice over a release manifest
criteria.scoring_only: Jev scores every candidate 0-3 on value; items above threshold auto-publish, borderline queued for human review
criteria.no_auto_publish: Jev only ranks/prioritizes; publishing is always human-triggered

auto_deploy_safety.instructions: Should a fully-gated pipeline be allowed to auto-deploy to production without a human click?

criteria.true: Yes: mechanical gates (build+check+links) plus Jev gates are enough for data updates (stars) and doc syncs
criteria.false: No: keep a human approval step for production deploys

frequency.instructions: What cadence for the scheduled runs?

criteria.daily: Daily fetch+gate cycle, deploy when gated changes accumulate
criteria.twice_weekly: Every 3-4 days: less noise, batches changes
criteria.weekly: Weekly: simplest, fine for a small doc site
criteria.hourly_stars: Hourly star refresh + weekly content cycle

where_new_content_lands.instructions: When new material passes the gate, where should it land first?

criteria.en_first: EN version first (en is the canonical fallback source), other languages fill in later via translation flow
criteria.zh_en_same: zh and en together (the two full languages), others follow
criteria.branch_pr: Automated branch + PR, merged after gates, so everything is reviewable in git history
